title: Projective and affine vanishing for Hodge ideals of rational divisors under reduced log canonicity
difficulty_reason: After treating the already-supported cyclic-cover, global filtered summand and logarithmic/direct-image computations of old1906 as given, the full original theorem still requires a generation-level bridge not proved in that old core. In the actually needed sufficient direction of Theorem10.1, the authors construct the multiplication morphism Phi_k, identify its kernel with locally free multiplication kernels, use new Corollary8.3 to annihilate higher direct images, and remove the exceptional lowest complex degree through B before obtaining the n-1 bound. This supports the high-k smoothness branch through multiplicity growth. The main proof then identifies a graded de Rham complex under reduced log canonicity, controls its endpoint using precise Nakano boundary vanishings, and replaces Saito vanishing by Artin plus filtered strictness in the affine branch. The kernel/truncation-to-generation bridge is the specific H2 burden; the old framework, standard vanishing theorems, number of cases and article prestige are not the difficulty basis.

source_disclosures: X is smooth projective of dimension n over the complex setting of the article; D is effective rational with reduced support Z.

Choose a positive integer ell such that ell D is integral, and retain the existence of M with M^ell isomorphic to O_X(ell D). Do not remove this root hypothesis; Remark12.2 explicitly says the general removal is not known for k>=1.
k is a nonnegative integer; reduced(k-1)-log-canonicity means I_0(D)=...=I_{k-1}(D)=O_X(Z-ceil D), equivalently I-prime_0=...=I-prime_{k-1}=O_X. The condition is vacuous for k=0.
Retain the initial L+Z-D ample condition exactly, and the precise subsequent positivity statement in branch(2); do not flatten the author wording into a new single positivity rule.
Branch(1): k<=n, L(pZ-ceil D) ample for every integer2<=p<=k+1 yields H^i=0 only for i>=2. H^1 additionally requires H^j(Omega_X^{n-j} tensor L((k-j+2)Z-ceil D))=0 for all1<=j<=k.
Branch(2): k>=n+1 forces smooth support through Corollary10.7; I_k(D)=O_X(Z-ceil D), and original L((k+1)Z-ceil D) ample yields all i>0.

Branch(3): U=X minus Z affine, L=M(-Z), with M(pZ-ceil D) ample for every1<=p<=k. The same applicable extra H^1 condition is retained. The proof uses the untwisted graded-DR vanishing obtained from Artin and strictness; it does not impose the incompatible original auxiliary ample twist A on this affine replacement.

Only original Theorem12.1 is the proposed primary. Corollary8.3, the needed generation bridge in10.1, Remark10.6 and Corollary10.7 are supporting, not additional counted units. Variants12.5/12.6 and Sections11/13–15 are not selected.
